quote: Corollary 4.1. Let X1 and X2 be two rv's with mean residual life (mrl) functions m1 and m2 and Harris family rv's Y1 and Y2 having mrl functions m∗1 and m∗2 , respectively, such that m1 (t)/m2 (t) increases in t. If X1 ≤mrl X2 , then Y1 ≤mrl Y2 provided that θ ≥ 1. The orders are reversed if m∗1 (t)/m∗2 (t) increases in t and 0 < θ ≤ 1.
compared: mrl-order preservation under increasing mrl ratio

hypotheses.text: m1/m2 increasing; θ ≥ 1 (forward) or m*1/m*2 increasing, 0 < θ ≤ 1 (converse)

conclusion.direction: X1 <=mrl X2 ⇒ Y1 <=mrl Y2 (θ ≥ 1); reversed for θ ≤ 1

ambiguity: Via mrl-ratio ⇒ hr and hr ⇒ mrl chains (S&S Thms 2.A.2, 1.D.1).

quote: Corollary 4.2. If X1 ≤Lorenz X2 , then Y1 ≤Lorenz Y2 provided that the function F2^{−1} (x)/F1^{−1} (x) is increasing for all x > 0.

Counterexample 4.1. Let X1 and X2 be two rv's having the Erlang distributions with survival functions F̄1 (x) = (1 + 2x)e−2x , F̄2 (x) = (x + 1)e−x and hazard rates rF1 (x) = 4x/(1 + 2x), rF2 (x) = x/(x + 1), for x > 0, respectively. So, X1 ≤hr↑ X2 . However, Figure 1 shows that for some 0 < θ < 1, t > 0 and some x > 0, rH1 (x + t; θ, k) ≯ rH2 (x; θ, k) or, equivalently, H̄2 (x; θ, k)/H̄1 (x + t; θ, k) is not increasing in x, i.e., the up hazard rate order is not preserved by transformation to the Harris family when 0 < θ < 1.
compared: failure of forward preservation of ≤hr↑ for θ < 1

quote: Theorem 3.2. Let Y1 and Y2 be rv's corresponding to the df's H(·; θ1 , k1 ) and H(·; θ2 , k2 ), respectively. If {0 < θ1 ≤ 1, θ2 ≥ 1} or {0 < θ1 ≤ θ2 , k1 = k2 = k}, then Y1 ≤lr Y2 .
compared: lr order between two Harris transforms of the same baseline across tilt parameters

quote: Theorem 4.1. X1 ≤st X2 if and only if Y1 ≤st Y2 .
model: Harris family, same tilt θ, k
compared: st-order preservation by Harris transformation (both directions)
ambiguity: By Theorem 3.1 of Abbasi–Alamatsaz–Cramer [1] at α = β.

quote: Remark 3.1. It is worth mentioning that, in view of our Theorem 3.2, Theorem 2.3 of [20] concerning the Marshall–Olkin family is not valid unless θ1 ≥ θ2 is replaced by θ2 ≥ θ1 .
compared: correction of an existing literature claim on tilt-parameter direction

conclusion.direction: literature result valid only with reversed tilt-parameter inequality

ambiguity: Also flagged in the introduction: 'Theorem 2.2 of [20] is valid only if the support of the tilt parameter is corrected. Hence, their result in Theorem 2.3 is not true.'
